text: In an ARP Cache Table, what does the FREE (F) state indicate?
info: FREE (F) = Empty / Expired, ready for new entry.

answers.text: An empty or expired entry ready to be overwritten
An entry waiting for an ARP Reply
A completed mapping between IP and MAC address
A full packet queue unable to send data

text: What does the PENDING (P) state in an ARP Cache Table represent?
info: PENDING (P) = Pending response (waiting for ARP Reply).

answers.text: The cache mapping is complete and valid
An ARP Request has been sent, and the system is waiting for an ARP Reply
An unused slot reserved for static mapping
The packet has successfully reached its destination

text: When ARP receives a MAC address and successfully pairs it with an IP address, what state does the entry transition to?
info: RESOLVED (R) = Resolved/Cleared, MAC address is fully resolved and ready to use.

text: What is the function of the Attempt field in an ARP Cache Table?
info: Attempt = Attempts count (number of ARP Requests re-transmitted).

answers.text: Counts down the time-to-live of the entry
Records the packet queue sequence number
Counts the number of packets waiting in queue
Tracks the number of times an ARP Request has been transmitted

text: What is the unit of measurement for the Time-out field in the ARP Cache Table, and what is its default initial value when transitioning to RESOLVED?
info: Initial Time-out = 900 seconds (15 minutes).

text: If an outgoing packet is waiting to be sent but the destination IP is still in the PENDING state, where is the packet stored?
info: State P = Packets must go to the Queue and wait.

answers.text: Stored in the Queue corresponding to that IP address
Saved to local hard disk storage

text: How is the Hardware Address field displayed in the ARP Cache Table while in the PENDING state?
info: PENDING = MAC unknown, so the Hardware Address field remains blank.

text: As time passes, which field value decreases for an entry in the RESOLVED state?
info: RESOLVED = Time-out counts down continuously.

text: In the RESOLVED state, which field becomes empty or hidden from the table?
info: Mapping obtained = No longer need to attempt requests (Attempt field cleared).

text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining an ARP Cache Table?
info: Cache = Remember mappings to avoid repeated Broadcast requests.

answers.text: To reduce redundant ARP Request broadcasts on the network
To resolve IP addresses into Domain Names

text: Which state in the ARP Cache Table allows the Output Module to immediately use the MAC address for frame encapsulation?
info: RESOLVED = Fully resolved and ready for data transmission.

text: If a destination IP queue contains 3 queued packets when the state transitions to RESOLVED, what happens to those packets?
info: State resolved = Release queued packets one by one.

answers.text: Transmits only the first packet and drops the rest
Combines all 3 packets into a single frame
Transmits all 3 packets sequentially (one by one)

text: In Example 3, when the Output Module receives an IP Datagram and experiences a Cache Miss, what is its initial action?
info: Cache Miss = Reserve slot -> set PENDING -> set Attempt = 1.

answers.text: Add a new entry with state PENDING and set Attempt = 1
Clear the entire Cache Table immediately
Send an ICMP Destination Unreachable error
Change the first entry's state to RESOLVED

text: In Example 3, when a Cache Miss occurs for a new IP, what packet type does the Output Module generate?
info: Unknown MAC = Broadcast an ARP Request.

text: In Example 4, which module receives the incoming ARP Reply packet and updates the Cache Table?
info: Incoming packet handling = Input Module.

text: When the Input Module receives an ARP Reply in Example 4, how does the IP state change in the cache table?
info: ARP Reply received = State changes from P (Pending) to R (Resolved).

text: In Example 4, upon updating the state to RESOLVED, what is the initial reset value for Time-out?
info: Newly RESOLVED = Reset Time-out counter to 900.

text: Which module periodically checks and updates Time-out and Attempt values in the Cache Table?
info: Background table maintenance = Cache-Control Module.

text: In Example 5, after 25 seconds elapse, why is the Time-out value of an existing RESOLVED entry reduced by 60 seconds?
info: Cumulative time: 20 + 15 + 25 = 60 seconds.

answers.text: Total cumulative time passed since example start reached 60 seconds (20s + 15s + 25s)
Extra time was deducted due to an incoming ARP Request

text: In Example 5, if the Time-out value of a RESOLVED entry reaches 0, what is the outcome?
info: Time-out = 0 -> Entry expires, state changes to FREE.

answers.text: State changes to FREE and the entry is removed

text: In Example 5, how does the Cache-Control Module handle the Attempt field for a PENDING entry on each periodic check?
info: Still PENDING on next cycle = Attempt count + 1.

text: If a PENDING entry's Attempt count exceeds the Maximum Attempts limit, what actions take place?
info: Max attempts exceeded = Give up -> set FREE, purge queue, send ICMP Error.

answers.text: State changes to FREE, queues are destroyed, and an ICMP Error is generated
Transmits packets without a MAC address

text: Which ICMP error message is sent back to the source host when ARP fails to resolve a target MAC address?
info: MAC resolution failed = Host Unreachable.

text: What is the process called when the Input Module removes queued packets and hands them to the Data Link Layer upon receiving an ARP Reply?
info: Put in queue = Enqueue / Remove from queue to send = Dequeue.

text: What does the acronym RARP stand for?
info: RARP = Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (opposite of ARP).

text: What is the primary function of the RARP Protocol?
info: ARP = IP -> MAC / RARP = MAC -> IP.

answers.text: Translates IP Address to MAC Address
Translates MAC Address to IP Address
Translates Domain Name to IP Address
Translates Port Number to IP Address

text: RARP was primarily designed to solve networking challenges for which type of device?
info: RARP is designed for Diskless Machines.

text: Why can't a Diskless Machine permanently store its assigned IP Address in its local ROM?
info: MAC address is fixed in ROM; IP changes by subnet and cannot be hardcoded in ROM.

answers.text: IP Addresses are network-dependent and assigned dynamically by Administrators
ROM chips are physically too large
An IP Address requires 6 bytes, exceeding ROM capacity

text: When a Diskless Machine boots up, what is the ONLY address it natively knows?
info: Booting a diskless host = Only knows its ROM MAC Address.

answers.text: MAC Address (Physical Address) burned into ROM

text: How is a RARP Request Packet transmitted across the physical network?
info: RARP Request = Broadcast (shouting because server location is unknown).

text: Why MUST a RARP Request be transmitted as a Broadcast?
info: RARP Server location unknown -> Must Broadcast.

answers.text: Because the requesting client does not know the location/address of the RARP Server
Because RARP Servers force broadcast communication

text: How is a RARP Reply Packet transmitted back to the client?
info: RARP Reply = Unicast (sent directly to the client).

text: Why CAN a RARP Reply be sent using Unicast?
info: Server knows client MAC from Request -> Can Unicast directly back.

answers.text: The RARP Server learned the client's MAC address from the incoming RARP Request
The server selects destination MAC randomly
It is required by IP Layer standards
The client provided its IP address beforehand

text: Which network entity looks up mapping tables and replies with an IP Address in a RARP system?
info: The RARP Server holds the MAC-to-IP binding table.

text: If a standard host (not a RARP Server) receives a RARP Request Packet, how does it handle it?
info: Not a RARP Server -> Discard / Ignore the frame.

answers.text: Replies with its own IP address
Saves the request info to its cache table

text: Which statement accurately describes the transmission direction of RARP messages?
info: Request = Broadcast / Reply = Unicast.

answers.text: Request is Unicast / Reply is Broadcast
Request is Broadcast / Reply is Broadcast
Request is Unicast / Reply is Unicast
Request is Broadcast / Reply is Unicast

text: How does the Packet Format of RARP compare to that of ARP?
info: RARP format = ARP format (differs only in Operation code).

answers.text: The structures are identical; they only differ in the Operation field value
RARP packets are twice the size of ARP packets
RARP lacks the Sender Hardware Address field

text: In a RARP Packet, what is the Operation field value when sending a RARP Request?
info: ARP Req = 1, ARP Reply = 2 / RARP Req = 3, RARP Reply = 4.

text: In a RARP Packet, what is the Operation field value when returning a RARP Reply?
info: RARP Reply = 4.

text: In a RARP Packet for an Ethernet Network, what is the length of the Hardware Length field in bytes?
info: Ethernet MAC address = 6 bytes (48 bits).

text: In a RARP Packet for IPv4, what is the length of the Protocol Length field in bytes?
info: IPv4 address = 4 bytes (32 bits).

text: In a RARP Request Packet, how is the Sender Protocol Address field filled?
info: Requesting host doesn't know its IP yet -> Sender Protocol Address is empty (0s).

answers.text: Populated with the RARP Server's IP
Populated with the Default Gateway's IP
Populated with the Broadcast IP address

text: Why is the Sender Protocol Address field left blank in a RARP Request Packet?
info: Unknown IP -> Leave blank to ask the server.

answers.text: The sender does not know its own IP address yet
The system forgot to populate it
The RARP Server forbids populating this field
The MAC address was inserted instead

text: What is the term for placing a RARP Packet into the Data field of an Ethernet Frame?
info: Placing payload into frame = Encapsulation.

text: In an Ethernet Frame encapsulating a RARP Packet, what hexadecimal value must be specified in the Type field?
info: Ethernet Type for RARP = 0x8035 (Standard ARP is 0x0806).

text: Ethernet Frame Type values 0x0806 and 0x8035 correspond to which protocols, respectively?
When a diskless host transmits a RARP Request Frame, what is specified in the Ethernet Frame's Destination Address field?
info: Data Link Layer Broadcast = FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.

text: What is the function of the 4-byte CRC field appended to an Ethernet Frame?
info: CRC = Checksum for frame-level Error Detection.

text: What is the most significant limitation of RARP that makes it insufficient for modern networks?
info: RARP gives IP only -> Missing Subnet Mask, Gateway, DNS.

answers.text: Data transmission speed is too slow
It provides only an IP address, failing to supply Subnet Mask, Gateway, and DNS settings
It cannot run on CAT6 cabling
It supports only Windows operating systems

text: Which essential networking parameters are required by a diskless host for inter-network communication, but CANNOT be supplied by RARP?
info: RARP lacks Subnet Mask, Default Gateway, and DNS.

answers.text: Subnet Mask, Router IP (Gateway), Name Server IP (DNS)

text: Which protocols were developed to overcome RARP's limitations by delivering comprehensive network configurations?
info: Protocols replacing RARP = BOOTP and DHCP.

text: What does the acronym BOOTP stand for?
info: BOOTP = Bootstrap Protocol.

text: At which layer of the OSI Model do BOOTP and DHCP operate?
info: RARP = Data Link/Network Layer; BOOTP & DHCP = Application Layer (uses UDP).

text: What major limitation of BOOTP makes it inconvenient for large-scale enterprise networks?
info: BOOTP = Requires Static (Manual) mapping tables.

answers.text: Supports a maximum of 10 IP addresses
Requires static pre-configured MAC-to-IP manual mapping

text: Which protocol currently serves as the dominant replacement for both RARP and BOOTP?
info: Modern standard for dynamic configuration = DHCP.

text: What is the key advantage of DHCP over BOOTP and RARP?
info: DHCP highlights = Dynamic IP allocation & Lease Time.

answers.text: Provides Dynamic IP allocation with configurable Lease Times
Transmits data without needing an IP address

text: Which parameter does a Diskless Workstation use to distinguish between Network ID and Host ID?
info: Separates Network ID and Host ID = Subnet Mask.

text: Why is a Default Gateway (Router IP) critical for a Diskless Workstation?
info: Default Gateway = Exit door to destination networks outside local LAN.

answers.text: Required to power on the machine
Acts as the exit path for sending packets outside the local LAN
Writes setup data directly to ROM
Converts MAC addresses to IP addresses

text: Which sequence correctly illustrates the chronological evolution of IP configuration protocols?
info: Evolution: RARP (Oldest) -> BOOTP -> DHCP (Current Standard).

text: Why is DHCP the most widely used network configuration protocol today?
info: DHCP = Full automation, complete configuration, zero manual admin effort.

answers.text: It is the only protocol that is completely free
It operates without requiring a server
It functions natively at the Data Link Layer
It automates full IP and network parameter assignment, significantly reducing administrative overhead
